utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just make a correction. This can be done in open session, Your Honours. The witness, on page 49, in line 9, said that it was a representative of the Red Cross from Zupanja and not from the canton, he mentioned the town of Zupanja. In the course of his testimony, he explained where that town is and this is quite important so I would like it to be quite clear in the transcript for this word to appear, Zupanja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, it will be corrected. Yes, about the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I indicated to the registrar that I needed to provide two pieces of information regarding the testimony of this witness, the Defence has two viva voce witnesses and then the accused Tadic should testify. We still have two witnesses by videolink in accordance with plan and your instructions we provided for the witness to come yesterday, Sveto Vasovic he arrived yesterday. I would also like to inform you that this is a witness for whom we have secured the personal escort or to be accompanied by his daughter. He has had three bypass surgeries but he did want to come and he felt capable of coming and testifying viva voce. What happened yesterday early in the morning at the Belgrade airport is that the computer system didn't work and it wasn't possible for him to go into the plane. We personally communicated with officials from Yugoslav Airlines and they placed him in the plane without a ticket but he did have a lot of problems with the administrative staff. When I spoke to him at 7.00 in the morning at Belgrade airport I found out that he wasn't feeling very well and then we immediately scheduled him to be seen by a doctor which was done yesterday and the doctor yesterday at the end of yesterday's session informed us that he cannot testified today at all and that he cannot also -- that we cannot also have any proofing sessions with him. My colleague Krgovic went to see him last night immediately and he expressed the wish to appear before the Chamber as soon as possible. He wanted to do that today but we had to respect the wishes of the doctor. My colleague Krgovic also went to see him today. He feels very well and we think, we cannot say that 100 per cent but we really believe and it is of importance for us for him to appear in the courtroom tomorrow. We still don't have any confirmation. Today he will also undergo another examination by the doctor but we are able at this point to confirm that tomorrow he should be able to appear to testify. The other witness, I did not -- I do not wish to state his name in open session, but I don't know what measures he will be requesting but you do have his information that I provided for you. This is a witness who was initially, if you remember, planned for depositions when we received your decision, we were already here and then by telephone, we communicated with him. The technical problems which existed at that point have now been surmounted, he didn't have a passport at all at the time, now he does have one and we have been informed that he could perhaps get a visa tomorrow. Technically it would be possible for him to be here on Friday, to come on the morning flight on Friday but what poses difficulties for us and I would like to hear the position of the Chamber on this right now, if this person arrives on Friday, the flight leaves Belgrade at 20 to 7.00 in the morning he could in The Hague at 11.00 a.m., we did not have any preparations with this witness for live testimony and we believe that it would not be possible to do such preparations in one hour. And then we would only have about one hour remaining because we are planning for Mr. Vasovic to be examined in chief all day tomorrow and half of Friday and then of course we would need time for cross-examination and re-examination as well so I would request the Chamber and this would be useful for the Defence as well and it would also be economical not to bring this witness now and interrupt his testimony. We could hear Vasovic first then when we finish with Vasovic, we could finish for the week. If the Trial Chamber insists, we will bring him on Friday to see if it's essential for him to come into the courtroom but we believe it will be very difficult for him just to hear him for one hour, not only that, but we need to inform the Prosecution of our notes as well so we think that this would be unfair to the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Besides the witness who is already here, whom you say has -- is a heart patient, the arrangements for the other witness whom you say is scheduled to arrive on Friday morning will be dealt with by the legal officer. The Trial Chamber will liaise with you with the legal officer possibly before the end of tonight or even tomorrow since he can only depart on Friday so you will able to make your arrangements. Regarding this witness whom you say has been to see the doctor and the doctor is of the view that he should be allowed to rest today, it's all right that he can rest and then we can hear him tomorrow but I would like to say to you, Mr. Lukic, that as you know that he is a heart patient, we would like to avoid a situation where he has to rest in between his testimony so please do stick to your summary, take him directly to the matters which are in issue which he is going to discuss and don't let him deal with peripheral matters. What I'm trying to say is let's use him as economically as possible to allow for his health so that he can finish as quickly as possible and they can he can go. Because your summaries are clear as to what he's going to discuss, yes, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, that's right, Your Honours. We will stick to our summaries completely and I informed the Prosecution that the only topics that we will deal with from the summary are the mention of the witnesses of the Prosecution, the witness, but everything will be a -- in accordance with the schedule that we have planned and I think so far we have kept to the schedule and did not exceed our allotted time so the Defence will be focussing on his work exclusively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: My concern is not about the hours. My concern is about his health so that we don't have a situation where he gives evidence half way then he has to go then come back another time. That's what I'm saying. So stick to your summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our wish -- I asked him, we knew about his health, we asked him whether he would prefer to testify by videolink or would he like to come and he expressed the wish to come and testify live so now that he's here, we do not want to interrupt his testimony, so we believe that we will be able to complete everything with this witness and there will be no need for him to come back at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Any other matters from the Prosecution at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has a ruling regarding the expert report by Dr. Leposava Kron. The Trial Chamber has considered the Prosecution motion to exclude the proposed Defence expert evidence of Dr. Leposava Kron, the joint Defence response to this motion and the Prosecution's subsequent reply have also been noted by the Trial Chamber. The report of Dr. Kron may be distinguished from the report of Dr. Stewart Turner filed in the Galic case on the basis that that latter report was tailored to the facts of the indictment whereas the report of Dr. Kron presents a general discussion of the psychology of war which has no relevance or probative value to the specific facts of this case. Dr. Kron's report does not consider the behaviour of the population of Bosanski Samac nor does it relate to any -- nor does it relate in a scientific study to the allegation of the persecution, deportation and transfer as laid out in the indictment. In accordance with Rule 89 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and notwithstanding Rule 94 bis the Trial Chamber may exclude evidence that is irrelevant and where it's probative value is substantially outweighed by the need to ensure a fair trial, the Trial Chamber therefore concludes that the report of Dr. Kron is irrelevant and bears no probative value to this case it is therefore excluded. The motion of the Prosecution is granted. As we cannot hear the next witness on account of his health, we shall adjourn and resume our proceedings tomorrow.
